title: FatterPad
tagline: The Thor's buttons are laid out like a Nintendo pad. Now Steam knows it.
insertQuote: The motion reader now uses 0.04% of a core between games, down from 3.7%.
what: Patches and a helper app that make Steam understand the AYN Thor's built-in controls: the right button icons for each game, a drawing of the real Thor in Steam's controller screens, and gyro aim in an emulator.
built: Patches so Steam sees the Thor as a Switch Pro Controller, updating about 221 times a second
A per-game switch: games that ship Nintendo icons get that layout, every other game gets Xbox
Drew the Thor into Steam's controller screens, including the live Test Device Inputs page
Gyro aim for the 3DS emulator, with drift correction while I hold the Thor
progress: Gyro aim is for the 3DS emulator.

remix.changed: A set of patches so the Thor shows up as a Switch Pro Controller, plus my own per-game layout switcher and motion reader.

making.problem: Steam saw a generic gamepad, so it drew the wrong buttons and had no idea the Thor could sense motion.
how: InputPlumber turns the Thor's controller into the virtual pads Steam sees; my patches make one of them a Switch Pro Controller.
A list of every game I own, with PCGamingWiki's answer on whether it ships Nintendo icons, decides the identity and layout when a game launches.
A small background program feeds the gyro to emulators, and only reads the sensor while something can use it.

broke.title: Quiet between games
broke.body: The motion reader now uses 0.04% of a core between games, down from 3.7%. It reads the sensor only while something can use it.

proof.caption: Steam's Test Device Inputs screen with the Thor drawn in.
Hades in Nintendo mode, drawing its own Switch icons.
The Thor on Steam's game-launch screen.

credits: Switch Pro protocol: nxbt, joycontrol, SDL and the Linux hid-nintendo driver
